records.text: Immediately He compelled His disciples to board the boat and go ahead to the other side, toward Bethsaida, while He Himself dismissed the crowd.
After saying farewell to them, He went away to the mountain to pray.
When evening came, the boat was in the middle of the sea, and He was alone on the land.
Seeing them straining at the rowing, for the wind was against them, He came toward them about the fourth watch of the night, walking on the sea. He intended to pass by them.
When they saw Him walking on the sea, they thought it was a phantom and cried out,
for they all saw Him and were troubled. Immediately He spoke with them and said to them, “Take courage! It is I; do not fear.”
He climbed into the boat with them, and the wind ceased. They were utterly astounded within themselves,
Lord my God, I cried out unto Thee, and Thou didst heal me.
Lord, Thou broughtest my soul up from Hades; Thou didst save me from those descending into a pit.
Sing praise to the Lord, His holy ones, and give thanks at the remembrance of His holiness,
Into Thy hands I will entrust my spirit; Thou didst redeem me, Lord, God of truth.
Thou didst hate those who guard vanities to no purpose; but I hoped in the Lord.
I will exult and rejoice in Thy mercy, because Thou didst look upon my humiliation; Thou didst save my soul from constraints
And the Lord’s word came to me, saying:
Can I not shape you as this potter does, house of Israel? Behold, you are like the potter’s clay in My hands.
At last I will speak concerning a nation or kingdom, to remove them and destroy,
and if that nation turns from all their evils, I will change My mind concerning the evils I planned to do to them.
And at last I will speak concerning a nation and kingdom, for it to be rebuilt and planted,
and if they do evil things before Me by not hearing My voice, I will change My mind concerning the good things I spoke of doing for them.
“And now,” says the Lord your God, “turn to Me with your whole heart, with fasting, weeping and mourning.”
Tear your hearts, not your garments, and turn to the Lord your God, because He is merciful and compassionate, patient and abundant in mercy, and relents concerning calamities.
Who knows whether He will turn and relent and leave a blessing behind Him, a sacrifice and drink offering for the Lord our God?
Blow a trumpet in Zion! Consecrate a fast; proclaim a service.
Gather the people; consecrate the congregation. Choose elders; gather infants nursing at breasts. Let the bridegroom leave his bedroom and the bride her bridal chamber.

In the midst of the altar’s platform the priests who minister to the Lord will weep and say, “Spare Thy people, Lord, and do not give Thine inheritance to reproach, for nations to rule over them, so that they do not say among the nations, ‘Where is their God?’”
The Lord descended in a cloud, stood beside him there, and called upon the name of the Lord.
The Lord passed before him and proclaimed, “The Lord God, compassionate and merciful, slow to anger, abundant in mercy and true,

preserving righteousness and showing mercy to thousands, taking away lawlessness, injustice, and sins, yet not cleansing the guilty, bringing the fathers’ lawlessness upon children and children’s children to the third and fourth generation.”
Ahab reported to Jezebel his wife all that Elijah had done, and how he had killed the prophets with the sword.
Jezebel sent to Elijah and said, “If you are Elijah, I am Jezebel! May the god do thus to me and add more, for at this time tomorrow I will make your life like the life of one of them!”
Elijah was afraid, rose, and went for his life. He came to Beer-sheba in Judah and left his young attendant there.

He himself went a day’s journey into the wilderness, came, and sat under a single broom bush. He asked that his life might end and said, “Let it be enough now! I pray Thee, take my life from me, Lord, for I am no better than my fathers.”
He lay down and slept there under a plant. Behold, someone touched him and said to him, “Rise and eat.”
Elijah looked, and there at his head were a hearth cake of spelt and a flask of water. He rose, ate, and drank, then lay down again.
The Lord’s angel returned a second time, touched him, and said to him, “Rise, eat, for the journey is too much for you.”
He rose, ate, and drank, and went in the strength of that food forty days and forty nights to Mount Horeb.

How shall I deal with you, Ephraim? Shall I shield you, Israel? How shall I deal with you? Shall I make you like Adama and like Seboim? My heart turned within itself; My change of mind was stirred together.
I will certainly not act according to My furious anger; I will certainly not abandon Ephraim to be erased. For I am God and not a human being, holy within you, and I will not enter a city.
Let the lowly brother boast in his exaltation,
and the rich person in his humiliation, because he will pass away like a flower of grass.
For the sun rose with its scorching heat and dried the grass, and its flower fell, and the beauty of its appearance perished. So also the rich person will wither in his pursuits.
O city of bloodshed, wholly false, full of injustice! Prey will not be touched.
The sound of whips and the sound of shaking wheels, of a pursuing horse and a jolting chariot,
and of a mounting horseman, a flashing sword and glittering weapons, a multitude of slain and a grievous fall! There was no limit to her nations, and they will weaken in their bodies
because of the multitude of prostitution. A prostitute, beautiful and pleasing, mistress of potions, selling nations through her prostitution and tribes through her potions,
Compassionate and merciful is the Lord, patient and abundant in mercy.
The Lord is kind to all, and His compassions are over all His works.
And the Lord said, “The cry of Sodom and Gomorrah has increased, and their sins are exceedingly great.
So I will go down and see whether they are being brought to an end according to their cry which comes to Me; and if not, that I may know.”
